subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `openclaw notify` admin broadcast surface now, fold shell-originated alerts into the broader WebUI notification architecture, or require this to live as a plugin/ClawHub package after a missing UI notification seam is defined?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent and useful, but it creates a new shell-facing admin capability and product-visible interruption surface across CLI, Gateway authorization, broadcast scoping, and Control UI UX.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the focused CLI/Gateway/Control UI contract and require explicit security and UX acceptance criteria before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broad Notification Tracker
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 canonical only after it explicitly covers shell/admin connected-UI broadcast semantics.

options.title: Externalize After Seam Decision
options.body: Reject a bundled root command and document a plugin/ClawHub route only if maintainers confirm current or new plugin UI seams can safely render connected-session notifications.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the focused CLI/Gateway/Control UI contract and require explicit security and UX acceptance criteria before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans current CLI, Gateway broadcast/security, Web Push, and Control UI event surfaces where current-main blame points to steipete's recent work.
